title: R' Chananiah bar Yehudah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In the Sifra, Tzav, on “This is the law of the meal-offering,” he challenged Rabbi Akiva and disagreed with him. In Shemini, on “Moses heard, and it was good in his eyes,” Rabbi Yehudah said: Chananiah ben Yehudah used to expound throughout his life, “Grave is anger, which caused Moses to err.” In [Yerushalmi Pesachim, chapter 5, halakhah 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.5.1.3), Rabbi Yosi said—as in the teaching: “Chananiah ben Yehudah says: I might understand ‘between the evenings,’” etc.[^1]

notes.text: The implicit subject of הקשה is the entry’s subject. קשה הקפדה judges the seriousness of anger or irritability; it is not the older draft’s disconnected “it is a difficult matter.” The heading’s bar and the quoted ben remain distinct. Hyman’s truncated final teaching is not completed with a new legal inference or verse. His Sifra references are still identified by their printed verse openings; the modern locators below are separately identified evidence.

The heading remains R' because Hyman abbreviates its title and the checked Sifra occurrence also abbreviates the title of Chananiah. The *Venice 1545* Sifra, Tzav, Section 2, paragraph 3, explicitly says רבי עקיבא and then records Chananiah’s challenge, supporting Rabbi Akiva at this occurrence. The same named edition at Shemini, Chapter 2, paragraph 12, explicitly has רבי יהודה with the anger teaching. Guggenheimer’s Jerusalem Talmud, Pesachim 5:1:3, explicitly has Rabbi Yosi before the Chananiah teaching. These exact title forms support the corresponding passages, without a global identity or era-based rule.
